narrative.overview: The interface is an instrument for reading and correcting money: precise, orderly and trustworthy. Figures are aligned in columns, units sit next to every amount, dates are written the same way everywhere, and what changed is always visible afterwards.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper surfaces, one ink-teal accent used for primary actions, the current navigation item and focus, and amber as the single second voice.
Right-aligned, tabular figures; sentence-case labels; amounts always followed by their currency code.
One shared page vocabulary: heading, one-sentence intro, filter row, data table, feedback blocks.
Meaning is never carried by colour alone: deviations carry a sign, statuses carry words.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Teal is the accent. It marks what can be acted on or what is current; it is never decoration. Amber is the only second voice and is reserved for "look at this".

rules.name: The Sign Before Colour Rule
rules.body: Anything coloured to mean above or below must also say it in text.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every table and definition list uses tabular numerals so amounts line up and do not jiggle when they change.

rules.name: The Both Schemes Rule
rules.body: A colour is never written as a literal in a component: it comes from a system token or a chart variable so both schemes stay in step.

dos: Do put the currency code after every amount and format with two decimals and thousands separators.
Do keep one vocabulary: the same filter row, table frame, banner and notice on every page.
Do keep keyboard focus visible on every control and link.
Do pair any colour meaning with a sign or a word.
donts: Don't add another accent colour beyond amber, or use teal as decoration.
Don't use shadows at rest on flat surfaces; reserve them for floating layers.
Don't introduce display fonts, gradients, glows or decorative motion in an operational screen.
Don't style a one-off control on a single page when a shared style exists.
